issues.description: The formative assessment evidence rationale is null rather than an explanatory string.
The formative assessment has scoring set to null, leaving the object shape less complete than other assessments.
The Practice and Assessment module has no lesson IDs or lesson objects, so the final 15 minutes are represented only at module level.

technical_review.notes: All listed objective, prerequisite, module, lesson, and assessment references resolve within the packet. Technical observations are kept separate from pedagogical judgement.

special_question.notes: Ignoring technical shape issues, the design is pedagogically reasonable: it moves from identifying missing/invalid values to transforming them and justifying decisions in a hands-on pandas task.

rubric_scores.rationale: The objectives include observable performances and criteria for identifying null/invalid values, applying transformation strategies, and justifying choices. The first objective is labeled understand even though the performance requires tool use, and some criteria need clearer thresholds.

The summative task measures identification, transformation, and justification in one realistic code-and-explanation performance. The formative task supports obj-1, though obj-2 and obj-3 have less explicit formative checking.

Correct issue identification, executable transformations, and written justifications are valid evidence for the target capability. Validity would be stronger if invalid value types, expected outputs, and analysis context were specified.

The transformation and justification objectives align with apply/evaluate demands, but identifying data issues using pandas is more apply/analyze than understand. The summative assessment cognitive label of apply under-represents the evaluative justification component.

The prerequisites are relevant and mostly minimal: basic Python, tabular structure, and pandas/library use. Pandas may need to be framed as candidate readiness or explicitly taught because the learner state confirms only basic Python.

The progression from detecting issues to transforming data to practice/assessment is sensible. Combining transformation and justification in Module 2 is efficient, though justification might need a clearer bridge from code choices to analysis goals.

Lessons support the summative task through demonstrations, worked examples, guided practice, and scenarios, but the final practice/assessment module has no lesson content and there is little guided preparation for the full integrated task.
Moderate under-teaching risk remains around invalid-value detection, choosing among transformation strategies, and writing defensible justifications within the available lesson detail.
The content is largely focused on the requested Python data-processing performance. There is little unnecessary breadth beyond including common pandas inspection and transformation methods.
Moderate edits are needed to adjust cognitive labels, specify invalid-value scope, complete formative scoring, and add final practice/assessment lesson detail.

prerequisite_acceptance.notes: All three prerequisites are relevant. Revisions should keep prereq-1 confirmed from learner_state.known, qualify prereq-2 as candidate tabular literacy, and decide whether prereq-3 pandas/library use is an entry requirement or part of instruction.

edit_effort.notes: Estimated edits include revising two cognitive/criteria statements, completing formative assessment rationale/scoring, clarifying two prerequisite statuses, and adding lesson-level support for the final practice/assessment segment.

pedagogical_review.overall_notes: A practical and mostly aligned draft for a 60-minute pandas cleaning activity, with moderate gaps in specificity and formative scaffolding.
